notes: Hermes variant of the 1-child orphan shape (the no-working-transition invariant is identical for any N>=1). A `hermes chat` parent dispatches ONE delegate_task subagent; hermes forces a top-level delegation to run in the BACKGROUND (delegate_tool.py's _model_background_value; the schema's `background` field is documented DEPRECATED/IGNORED), so the tool returns a handle immediately and the child keeps running on a module-level DaemonThreadPoolExecutor. The child is a THREAD in the parent's process, and it persists its own `sessions` row into the SAME $HERMES_HOME/state.db with parent_session_id = the parent's id (AIAgent._ensure_db_session in run_agent.py, fed by session_db + parent_session_id at delegate_tool.py:~1390). That row is tagged source='subagent' (platform="subagent" -> _session_source_for_agent's platform fallback; corroborated by hermes' own tools/session_search_tool.py _HIDDEN_SESSION_SOURCES), which irrlicht's watcher dropped until commit 6ad7c28a widened Watcher.scanSessions to source IN ('cli','tui','subagent'). The recipe then SIGKILLs the single hermes process while the child is still inside its `sleep 90`, so the child is orphaned rather than reaped by its own clean exit. Both sessions bind the SAME pid (the child row carries no cwd -- _launch_cwd_for_session returns None for source != 'cli' -- so the watcher's live-process cwd fallback gives it the parent's cwd, which DiscoverPID resolves to the parent's PID; assignPIDLocked exempts subagents from same-PID staleness so the child does not evict the parent). When the PID vanishes, HandleProcessExit fires per watched session: process_exited then deleteWithChildren, which is a pure repo.Delete + broadcast with NO SetState -- so no state_transition can fire for the orphan during cleanup (issue #321). Birth is TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: a transient proc-<PID> presession is minted at launch and the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message; every post-birth parent phase is anchored to the REAL session. Delays are generous because the store is polled (2s backstop) rather than inotify-driven and the child's row only appears on its first flush. Observations pin neither model nor cost: the recording home's model is a human choice, and irrlicht's alias table has no price entry for the locally configured model (EstimateCostUSD returns 0) while hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under subscription billing -- tokens_nonzero is safe because the sessions row carries input/output aggregates. Invariants use the BARE DSL form `no state_transition to <state>`, the only form validate/expected.go's invariantNoStateRE parses (the opencode sibling's longer prose invariants are silently skipped); the check is session-scoped to the matched event, i.e. the orphaned child.

text: The transient proc-<PID> presession minted by the process scanner appears in ready (hermes declares a ProcessMatcher, so this row exists before any store row does)
The REAL parent hermes session (a distinct id, shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>, from the sessions row INSERTed on the first user message) appears in ready
The user prompt drives the parent session ready -> working; the turn's only tool call is the single delegate_task dispatch

The delegate child materializes as its OWN session -- a sessions row written into the shared store while the child is live, with parent_session_id set and source='subagent'. Hermes writes no child transcript file; the store row is the only trace.
The detector binds child.session_id -> parent.session_id (hermes' subagent-spawn proof; the recorded session_id is the CHILD's)

The SIGKILL orphans the in-flight child (still inside its `sleep 90`); the sweep reaps it via process_exited and NEVER resurrects it into working or waiting -- the issue #321 invariant, scoped to the orphan's own session_id
The same SIGKILL reaps the parent: the PID both sessions share is gone, so pid_manager records process_exited for the parent session too
